title: Evaluation of different strategies to address postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) via acupuncture - APONVA a randomized controlled pilot trial
summary:
The APONVA study is a randomized controlled pilot trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of acupuncture in the prevention and treatment of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) following laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

Four groups are compared: classical acupuncture needles, auricular acupuncture, acupressure wristbands, and standard treatment (control/placebo group).

The aim of the study is to investigate whether acupuncture can serve as an effective alternative or adjunct to conventional PONV management by reducing the severity and incidence of symptoms and potentially decreasing the need for antiemetic medication. This approach may contribute significantly to improving postoperative care and enhancing patients' quality of recovery and overall well-being.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy 

Sufficient communication skills  

Apfel-Score ≥3.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing body parts for acupuncture (e.g. extremities) or infection or malignant tumor at the site of needle placement  

Needle phobia  

Relevant mental disorders (e.g. borderline patients with a risk of self-harm, posttraumatic disorders, relevant depression)  

Serious coagulation disorders (e.g.: clinically relevant hemophilia)  

Neurological disorders (e.g. polyneuropathy, apoplexy)   

Autoimmune disease affecting the skin
